meta.hazardAnalysis:
Daily operations may take safety personnel to various locations which contain hazards with little or no time to return to the office to collect appropriate PPE. PPE must be taken with the employee and used when necessary when conducting work outside the office.
      - Foot hazards: PPE issued: Safety/steel-toe footwear 
      - Head hazards: PPE issued: Hard hat. Clean with mild soap and water.
      - Hearing hazards: Personnel are not on a hearing conservation program, but may enter areas where loud noise is present. Hearing protection (hard shell and disposable-type are provided in the work center. Clean hard shell ear muffs with mild soap and water. 
      - Hand hazards: PPE Issued: leather, nitrile, or mechanics-style gloves. Dispose of nitrile gloves in approved trash containers.
      - Eye hazards: PPE issued: ANSI Z87.1 glasses. Clean with eye glass wipes. If contaminated with hazardous chemicals, dispose of them in approved containers and optain a new pair from the supervisor.
      - Night time/Reduced visibility traffic exposure: PPE Issued: Reflective vest and/or belt. Reflective vest or belt will be worn over the outer most garment when the employee is exposed to a traffic environment (i.e. roadways, flightline, etc) during hours of darkness or reduced visibility.

meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
JBMDL Speed limit if not otheriwse posted = 25mph. Do not speed. Obey the rules of the road when responding to a mishap. Remember you are NOT a first responder and must obey all traffic rules and regulations. 

Vehicle operators should pay their full attention to the operation of the vehicle. All drivers must follow applicable federal, state, local and host nation laws that are more stringent than this guidance on distractions while driving (e.g., using cellular phones, text messaging).

On base all traffic circles are one lane. Traffic entering the circle must yield to traffic in the circle. When exiting the circle use your turn signals.

Jug-handles are used extensively off base but not on base. No two jug-handles are the same. Be alert for other drivers who may cut you off trying to make their turn. If you miss your turn at a jug-handle do not cut off other drivers. Instead, continue down the road until you can safely go back.

You can expect seasonal heavy fog, typically in Autumn. Reduce driving speeds and use your headlights. 

New Jersey “Wipers On, Headlights On” Law
In New Jersey, you must have your headlights on whenever your windshield wipers are in use, regardless of whether it’s day or night, and regardless of the amount of precipitation.

When Headlights Are Required
      1) From half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise — even in clear weather.
      2) Whenever you use your windshield wipers — this includes light drizzle, rain, snow, mist, or any other moisture that triggers wiper use.
      3) When visibility drops below 500 feet due to fog, smoke, or other adverse conditions.

Passing on the Right in New Jersey. In New Jersey, passing on the right is generally prohibited unless specific safety conditions are met. 

When Passing on the Right is Permitted, only if:
      1) The vehicle ahead is making or about to make a left turn and there is enough unobstructed pavement to do so safely.
      2) The roadway has two or more substantially continuous lines of traffic moving in the same direction, allowing a lane change to the right.
      3) On one-way streets, if the road is wide enough for two or more lines of traffic and free of obstructions.
      4) In all these cases, you must pass at a safe distance to the left and not drive off the pavement or main-traveled portion of the road to complete the maneuver.

When Passing on the Right is Prohibited. Passing on the right is illegal in most other situations, including:
      1) When there is only one lane of traffic in the same direction.
      2) When the vehicle ahead is not making a left turn.
      3) When it is not safe to pass (e.g., hills, curves, intersections, railroad crossings, narrow bridges, or “No Passing” zones).
      4) Anywhere on JBMDL unless the roadway has a left turn lane allowing the right lane to continue moving.

The JB MDL Clinic does not provide emergency services.  For any severe or life threatening injury call 911 for an ambulance (NOTE: let the operator know you are on Joint Base McGuire Dix Lakehurst you will be transferred to the on base call center).  

Non-emergency: 
      1) During normal duty hours on weekdays (0800-1600), personnel should report to JB MDL Occupational Medicine Clinic (McGuire) for assessment and treatment of non-emergency injuries suffered while on-the-job.  Civilian employees may elect to receive treatment from their personal physician.  
      2) If injuries are non-life threatening injuries, or injuries suffered during other than normal duty hours, go to the emergency room at Deborah (Browns Mills).

Emergency Medical Facilities.
      1) Deborah Heart and Lung Center; 20 Pine Mill Road, Brown Mills, NJ 08015 (609) 283-9019.

selectedModules.title: Manual Material Handling (bending, lifting, twisting)
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document the local task or hazard, identify where the training is located, and explain how completion is documented.
selectedModules.notes:
Back injuries are a significant cause of disability, with 75% of workplace-related back injuries occurring during lifting tasks. Following these guidelines can help minimize the risk of strains, sprains, fractures, and other injuries.

Preparing for the Lift. Before you even touch the object, it is crucial to plan ahead.
      - Assess the Load. Test the weight of the object to ensure it is manageable. If it is too heavy or bulky, get assistance from a coworker or use mechanical aids like a dolly or hand truck. 
      - Clear Your Path. Ensure the route you will take is free of obstacles, debris, and is not slippery. Know where you will place the object before you lift it. 
      - Warm-Up. Just like any other physical activity, it is important to warm up your muscles before lifting. Simple stretches for your back and legs can help prevent injuries. 

Proper Lifting Technique. The way you lift an object is critical to protecting your back and preventing injury. The goal is to use your legs, not your back.

      - Get Close to the Load. Stand as close to the object as possible. The closer the load is to your spine, the less force it exerts on your back. 
      - Maintain a Stable Stance. Keep your feet shoulder-width apart, with one foot slightly in front of the other for better balance. 
      - Bend at Your Knees and Hips. Squat down by bending your hips and knees, keeping your back straight. Avoid bending forward. 
      - Keep Your Back Straight. Maintain the natural curve of your lower back. Look straight ahead and keep your shoulders back. 
      - Grip the Load Securely. Get a firm grip on the object before lifting. 
      - Lift with Your Legs. Straighten your legs to lift the object, keeping your back straight. Avoid jerking or snatching the load. 
      - Keep the Load Close. Hold the object close to your body, at about waist level. 

Carrying and Setting Down the Load. The process of carrying and setting down the object is just as important as the lift itself.

      - Avoid Twisting. Use your feet to change direction, taking small steps. Do not twist your body while holding a heavy object. 
      - Maintain Clear Vision. Make sure you can see over or around the load you are carrying. 
      - Set Down Safely. To set the object down, reverse the lifting process. Squat down by bending your knees and hips, keeping the load close to your body and your back straight. 

When to Use Mechanical Aids. For heavy, bulky lifting tasks, always consider using hand trucks.

By following these ergonomic principles, you can significantly reduce your risk of injury when lifting and moving objects. Remember, no single technique is perfect for every situation, so it is important to adapt these principles to the specific task at hand.

selectedModules.title: Slips, Trips, & Falls
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document the local task or hazard, identify where the training is located, and explain how completion is documented.
selectedModules.notes:
Water may puddle around doors and walking surfaces during periods of heavy rainfall.  This often causes the tile just inside the building doors to become wet.  
      - Do use handrails.  
      - Do watch where you are walking.
      - Do use extreme caution when entering and exiting the building.  The wet tiles cause your boots to be slippery when you step onto the floor at once inside the building.
      - Do not carry items stacked above eye level up or down stairs.  
      - Do not read or text while going up or down stairs.  
      - If wearing cleats in the winter remove them upon entering buildings.

selectedModules.title: Seasonal Weather
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document the local task or hazard, identify where the training is located, and explain how completion is documented.
selectedModules.notes:
High temperatures during summer months.  Drink plenty of fluids.  Be aware of symptoms of heat exhaustion: skin is clammy and moist, fatigue, giddiness, nausea, and headache.  If you or a coworker experience any of these symptoms the victim should rest in a cool place and drink water or an electrolyte solution.  

Heat stroke:  body stops sweating, mental confusion, delirium, loss of consciousness, convulsions or coma, body temp of 106 degrees or higher, hot dry skin which may be red, mottled, or bluish.  Seek medical attention at once.  

During the winter months it can get quite cold and you should always wear the proper clothes. It is your responsibility to ensure you have the right foul weather gear at work.

If you are working outdoors and there is a warning of lightning in the area go indoors or into a vehicle. Listen to the Giant Voice for further instructions.

South New Jersey has a very large pine forest. There is a year-round fire danger. If you smoke, be very mindful of where you smoke and how you dispose of your smoking materials.

selectedModules.title: Bloodborne Pathogens
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document the local task or hazard, identify where the training is located, and explain how completion is documented.
selectedModules.notes: Your job does not typically require you to handle contaminated materials. If you are exposed to another person’s blood or other bodily substances let your supervisor know and report to the occupational medicine clinic at the 87 MDG.

selectedModules.title: Airfield Driving
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document the local task or hazard, identify where the training is located, and explain how completion is documented.
selectedModules.notes:
The airfield/Flightline is a hazardous environment. DO NOT operate any vehicle on the airfield/Flightline unless you are licensed to do so. 

Always wear your reflective vest/belt when on the airfield/Flightline in reduced visibility.

Be mindful of vehicles and aircraft movement. Aircraft have the right-of-way.

selectedModules.title: Unexploded Ordnance
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document the local task or hazard, identify where the training is located, and explain how completion is documented.
selectedModules.notes:
The Dix ranges have been in use for one hundred years. There are UXOs on the ranges and on some areas of Lakehurst. DO NOT go down range on any range without first checking in with Range Control. 

RECOGNIZE, REREAT, REPORT. Recognize the potential UXO, Retreat to a safe location, and Report it to SFS.

selectedModules.title: Tick-borne Illness
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document the local task or hazard, identify where the training is located, and explain how completion is documented.
selectedModules.notes:
New Jersey has an abundance of ticks and they can be found outdoors and indoors. Deer ticks may carry Lyme Disease. If you are bitten by a tick at work first carefully remove the tick being careful not to break its jaws off as you remove it.  Keep the tick and notify your supervisor. You can take the tick to the public health clinic at the 87 MDG where they may be able to test the tick for Lyme Disease. Keep an eye on the bite site for several days. If you see a rash or bulls-eye shaped mark notify your doctor and your supervisor.

Alpha-gal syndrome is a food allergy to red meat and other products made from mammals.  A Lone Star tick bite can transmits a sugar molecule called alpha-gal into the person’s body.  This can trigger an immune system reaction that produces mild to severe allergic reactions to red meat.

selectedModules.title: Ergonomics
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document the local task or hazard, identify where the training is located, and explain how completion is documented.
selectedModules.notes: Repetitive tasks such as typing may create physical problems in some individuals.  To avoid such problems, alternate your tasks to prevent the over-exertion of a particular body part or series of parts.  Your job provides you the latitude to alternate tasks without hindering mission effectiveness. Standing desks are available to provide reflief from prolonged sitting.
